enforcement_disclosure.summary: These rulesets are a SIGNAL, not a block. Red means look at this; it does not mean you cannot proceed.
why: Every in-scope repo sets bypass_actors = [{RepositoryRole: 5 (admin), bypass_mode: always}], kept deliberately so the owner retains the override (#288).
The owner is admin on every one of these repos, so no rule here binds the owner. A PR can show BLOCKED and still be merged.
An agent that reads 'protected default branch' and infers that a red check stops a merge has inferred something false, and will make decisions on it.
This text is printed by repo-gate on every run because an undocumented signal is worthless, and because the disclosure is easy to lose if it lives only in a doc nobody opens.
enforcement_disclosure.what_is_actually_enforced: Nothing, against the owner. Against a hypothetical non-admin collaborator: no branch deletion, no force-push, and changes must arrive via a pull request.

scope.rule: Public non-fork repos owned by duppypro, plus private repos created in 2026.
scope.target_why: 6 in-scope repos default to `master`, not `main`. Targeting the literal name would silently govern 23 of 29 and report the other 6 as compliant-by-absence.
scope.excluded_why: Named one by one rather than left to a filter, so that dropping a repo out of governance is a visible edit to this file instead of a silent consequence of a predicate.

pull_request_parameters_not_pinned.allowed_merge_methods: repo-local preference; princess-pi-packages squash-merges via pr-merge, others may not
pull_request_parameters_not_pinned.require_code_owner_review: inert; no CODEOWNERS in any in-scope repo
pull_request_parameters_not_pinned.why: A baseline that pins fields it does not mean turns every cosmetic difference into a red row, and a report that cries wolf stops being read. Only fields carrying intent are asserted.

gated.description: Baseline plus a required CI check. Only for repos that actually ship a test suite — requiring a check no workflow produces leaves the branch permanently pending.

protected.description: Baseline only: no deletion, no force-push, changes via pull request. The resting state for a repo with no test suite to gate on.

plan-blocked.description: Private repo on an account plan that does not offer rulesets. Expected state is ZERO rulesets. This is not drift and must never be reported as a failure.
plan-blocked.waiver_why: Asserted as still-necessary rather than merely tolerated: repo-gate re-checks the account plan on every run, and the moment private rulesets become available these 12 repos go red on their own. A waiver that cannot expire is indistinguishable from a blind spot.

tier_history.update_rule_dropped: Until 2026-08-15 the 16 `protected` repos carried `update` (only bypass actors may update matching refs) instead of `pull_request`. `pull_request` subsumes the one property `update` held — a non-bypass actor cannot update the ref — while `deletion` and `non_fast_forward` cover the rest independently. Collapsing to one baseline removed a two-dimensional difference between tiers that nobody had chosen (#288).
tier_history.plan_blocked_waiver_never_applied: Until 2026-08-16 these 12 private repos were tiered `plan-blocked`, excused from carrying any ruleset: agentic-arts-ai, big-thoughts, btw, circuitpython, crispyhardware-com, dotfiles-doctor, duppy-com, interfacearts-com, portfolio-api, princess-pi-agent-workspace, princess-pi-brain, rogue-savvy. The waiver was FALSE the whole time. GitHub offers private-repo rulesets on paid plans and this account is `pro`; the waiver survived only because `/user` omits `.plan` unless the token holds `user`/`read:user`, which it did not. repo-gate reported the probe as `indeterminate` — held but unverified — on every run, so the tier stood on an assumption nobody could check. Granting `read:user` resolved the probe to `pro` and the waiver expired on its own, exactly as tiers.plan-blocked.waiver_why promised. Re-tiered to `protected`, not `gated`: gated adds required_status_checks, and demanding checks of a repo with no CI blocks every merge. The plan-blocked tier keeps its definition with zero members so the waiver machinery survives a future downgrade (#299).
